page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-4-lssd is an arm64-based server instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It is configured with 4 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, ensuring dedicated compute allocation. The memory subsystem provides 32.0 GB of RAM, translating to 8.0 GB per core, supported by an 80 MB L3 cache. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 402 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results indicate average overall performance across standard workloads. The Neoverse-V2 processor achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1818.99 and a multi-core score of 7256.38. Memory performance is a notable strength, with a PassMark memory score categorized as strong and a read-only cached small block bandwidth of 494.32 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression is also strong at 32.26 GB/sec. However, cryptographic performance is poor, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 834.19, and LLM inference speeds are weak to poor, particularly for 7B models.

Given its 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, this instance offers a resource-dense profile for memory-bound and storage-sensitive tasks without the overhead of x86 licensing. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and software compilation. It is less suitable for heavy cryptographic workloads or large language model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-4-lssd is an arm64-based server instance powered by a 3.0 GHz ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores and no hyperthreading. It features a memory-optimized configuration of 32.0 GB RAM (8.0 GB per core) and includes a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD. Benchmarks show strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and cached read bandwidth of 494.32 GB/sec, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression. However, cryptographic and LLM inference capabilities are weak. This instance provides a cost-efficient, resource-dense profile for memory-intensive and local storage-dependent workloads. It is highly suitable for database operations, Redis caching, static web serving, and software compilation, while being less optimal for compute-heavy encryption tasks.
